request.label: dev-digest-intro
request.system: You write short, plain, honest prose for a developer audience about the Business Central launch event. Use only the facts given. No em-dashes, no bullet lists, no headings, no hype words. Return JSON { "text": "..." } with paragraphs separated by blank lines.
request.prompt:
Write the introduction (3 short paragraphs, 120 to 180 words total) of a "developer digest" for Business Central AL developers about the 2026 release wave 2 launch event. Tone: direct, a bit of humor, no corporate fluff, no hype adjectives, no em-dashes. Say what themes dominate for developers and what to watch first. Use only the feature list below; do not add facts. Status rule for this event: a feature is generally available unless the presenters said otherwise; "(implied)" means nothing was said, so do not call those "unclear". Do not list features one by one, the list follows your text. Do not use headings.

Features with high developer relevance (67, about 108 minutes of video):
- Namespaces in translation IDs (GA (implied), 7 min, Developer tools): XLIFF files can use fully qualified names including the namespace as ids instead of hash keys. This avoids collisions between same-named objects in different namespaces and makes ids readable.
- Keys spanning base and extension fields (GA (implied), 7 min, Developer tools): Because table extensions are merged into the base table, a key or index can cover both base table and table extension fields. This was a long-requested item.
- AL language server for agents (GA (implied), 7 min, Developer tools): A standalone AL language server gives project-aware language intelligence over the language server protocol, not tied to Visual Studio Code. Agents resolve definitions, references, types, implementations and callers instead of relying on text search.
- Profiling MCP for agents (GA (implied), 6 min, Developer tools): A coding agent can start, monitor and stop a sampling profile through the AL tool proxy or the Business Central MCP server, given a session ID. It returns CPU profile files and an overview of duration, SQL and HTTP calls, and the demo found a background codeunit producing 30,000 rows.
- Telemetry-triggered snapshot capture (GA (implied), 6 min, Developer tools): The agent arms snapshot debugging, sets snap points and polls telemetry for a specific error. When found it downloads the snapshot and reasons about the root cause.
- Integer to big integer field change (GA (implied), 6 min, Developer tools): A field can change from integer to big integer while keeping existing rows, aimed at entries that run out of numbers. The compiler and AppSourceCop warn about implicit conversions and overflow, but the change is allowed without copying data.
- MCP data tools (GA (implied), 5 min, Copilot and agents): Four system tools (find tables, table relations, table schema, data query) let an LLM write AL queries that Business Central compiles and runs, with no APIs needed. Compiler errors return to the agent so it can correct itself.
- AL graph (GA (implied), 5 min, Developer tools): A graph command in the AL tool builds a static call graph across an extension and its dependencies. You or an agent can query who calls whom, external integration points, and public entry points.
- BC-Bench code review category (GA (implied), 5 min, Developer tools): A category tests whether AI can review AL changes against an expected comment. An LLM judge scores whether generated comments match.
- Mirroring to Microsoft Fabric (preview, 4 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Business Central data is synchronized live into OneLake through an open mirroring database. Setup is three steps: mirror database, connect, choose tables and companies.
- Public package resources (GA (implied), 4 min, Developer tools): Resource folders can be marked public so other apps can list and read them as JSON or text by provider app ID, without a dependency. Private resources still work with the normal functions without an app ID.
- Data-driven tests (GA (implied), 4 min, Developer tools): One test procedure can run against many data sets from a test data source, so more tests come from adding data points. The platform runs the test once for every entry, building the data on demand.
- AL MCP environment symbol search (GA, 3 min, Developer tools): The AL MCP can search the connected environment and tell which app and version owns each object. The symbol search tool has a source parameter set to environment, so symbols are looked up on the server without downloading them or setting dependencies.
- Snapshot debugging MCP for agents (GA (implied), 3 min, Developer tools): Agents can target an environment and start a snapshot recording for the next matching session, capturing values and call stacks. The agent analyzes the results and can place better snap points and re-arm until the cause is found.
- Agentic slow SQL analysis via telemetry (GA (implied), 3 min, Developer tools): An agent watches telemetry for slow SQL calls, finds the session and starts sampling. Its verdict identified an index issue with root causes and fixes.
- BC-Bench evaluation framework (GA (implied), 3 min, Developer tools): A reproducible open-source framework evaluates AI coding agents on real AL tasks from real PRs and tests. It measures the impact of model, tool, instruction and agent changes.
- Default implementation for interface methods (GA (implied), 3 min, Developer tools): Interface methods can have a default implementation, so implementers do not have to implement newly added methods. Consumers get a warning that a default exists and can still implement their own logic.
- PTE lifecycle management in the admin center (GA (implied), 3 min, Admin and platform): Upload, install and update operations are added to PTE management in the admin center, bringing full PTE lifecycle management into one place. Installs start from the apps page with an install extension button.
- Multiple scheduled PTE installs and cancel (GA (implied), 3 min, Admin and platform): Several future installs can be scheduled for the same PTE, for example one version on the next minor and another on the next major update. Scheduled installs show on the app details page and can be canceled before they run.
- Test handlers (GA (implied), 3 min, Developer tools): Test handlers provide setup and tear down in AL, with hooks before and after the test codeunit, test procedure and each data-driven test case. The demo uses a logger handler that traces while tests run.
- Composite layouts (GA (implied), 2 min, Reporting and analytics): The old all-in-one report layout is split into a body layout for structure, a theme for look and feel, and a header footer layout. Theme and header footer are applied at runtime, so the same report can be run in different ways.
- Component supply method on BOM lines (GA (implied), 2 min, Supply chain): A field on production BOM lines sets how a component reaches the subcontractor: transfer, consignment at vendor, or vendor supplied.
- Table extensions stored on base table (GA (implied), 2 min, Developer tools): Table extension fields are stored on the base table, so no join is needed. Reads are faster and writes up to 30% faster in a benchmark.
- Report inbox APIs (GA (implied), 2 min, Reporting and analytics): New APIs cover the report inbox operations, where scheduled reports and report packs land. Agents and automation can use them to trigger processing or AI analysis, through Power Platform, an MCP server, Copilot Studio or any API client.
- Business Central MCP server as data access layer (GA (implied), 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Copilot gets Business Central data through the same MCP server used for agentic integration. It reaches all tables, including extensions, without custom APIs.
- Default test handlers (GA (implied), 2 min, Developer tools): Regular test handlers are declared by the test codeunit, while default handlers run on every test, including tests from other apps. They suit telemetry setup or running Microsoft test suites against your extension.
- Updated data picker (GA (implied), 2 min, Reporting and analytics): The Word add-in data picker got UX improvements. It shows the company information data set next to report information.
- Run BC-Bench on your own data set (GA (implied), 2 min, Developer tools): Partners can fork the open-source repo and use their own bug fixes, tests and PRs. Contamination should be checked for open-source repos.
- Non-debuggable boundary audit (GA (implied), 2 min, Developer tools): A query finds debuggable callees of non-debuggable methods, where a breakpoint could leak content.
- AL code review approaches (GA (implied), 2 min, Developer tools): BC-Bench compares plain Copilot CLI, BC Quality as a plug-in and the AL review agent. The review agent focuses on security, privacy and performance and already comments on BC apps PRs.
- Test data source interface (GA (implied), 2 min, Developer tools): An interface with one function to list test cases and one to build test context objects. Sources can be resource files, generated cases, tables or web services.
- Company information data set (GA (implied), 1 min, Reporting and analytics): A company information data set is always shipped with Word layouts, so authors need not add it themselves. It is useful for header and footer layouts.
- Agentic developer loop (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): The agent plans an investigation and uses ALSP, the AL tool proxy and the Business Central MCP server for call stacks, variables and CPU profiles. The loop is understand, capture, measure, fix.
- AL MCP server for coding agents (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): The AL MCP server exposes compile, publish and search to agents without VS Code. It improved pass@5 by almost 10% in BC-Bench at the cost of longer runs.
- Required pending attribute (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): An attribute tells interface consumers that implementing a new method will become mandatory in a later major. Consumers get a warning instead of a break.
- Address design control (GA (implied), 1 min, Reporting and analytics): A design block offers three address formats, such as sender, receiver and shipping address in three columns.
- Update a PTE from the admin center (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): From the app details page you can install a different version of an installed PTE. This triggers an update rather than a new install.
- HTTP client caller query (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): A query exports everything calling the HTTP client, excluding tests, as a call path tree.
- Deprecation of in-environment PTE management (announced, 1 min, Admin and platform): PTE management in the extension management pages and in the automation API will be deprecated as of version 30.0. Users should migrate to the admin center within about half a year and not mix both experiences in one environment.
- Dev extensions remain installed on sandboxes (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): Dev extensions are treated more like PTEs and are not uninstalled during environment updates or other lifecycle operations unless incompatible. This reduces unexpected uninstalls and republishing.
- AL graph meta model extraction (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): An extract subcommand builds a JSON meta model of caller-callee relationships once. Later queries run against it.
- Connecting to the snapshot debugging MCP server (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): Connect through the AL tool as MCP host, Visual Studio Code via launch.json starting the snapshot MCP proxy, or your own MCP host.
- Table builder editing (GA (implied), 1 min, Reporting and analytics): The table builder can edit an existing table definition through the wizard, not only insert tables.
- Test handler registration via enum extensions (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): Handlers are registered by extending the test handler enum for opt-in or the default test handler enum for global.
- Hide if control (GA (implied), 1 min, Reporting and analytics): A content control hides or shows its content based on a chosen boolean value.
- Deployment schedules for PTE installs (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): When installing a PTE you can choose immediate, next minor update or next major update, plus a sync mode. Previously in-product installs could only be immediate.
- Get next object ID tool (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): An MCP tool reads app.json, works out the ID ranges and suggests free object IDs. In the demo it skipped IDs already in use.
- Field group design control (GA (implied), 1 min, Reporting and analytics): A design block for label and value pairs as a column grid, single or double stacked. It will be used in new body layouts.
- TestHandlers property (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): A test codeunit property takes a comma-separated list of handlers. A codeunit can implement the interface and register itself.
- Data-driven tests in Test Explorer (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): After one run, all test cases appear in the VS Code Test Explorer. Running selections and debugging work as usual.
- Configuration packages for Fabric tables (preview, 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Configuration packages define tables to synchronize, for example for the Power BI apps. ISVs can ship their own package.
- Command line test run with JSON output (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): The whole test suite can be run from the command line. It returns structured JSON with pass, fail and skip counts and a real exit code, so failures fail the build.
- Themes and header footer layouts from AL (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): In the rendering section of a report you specify type Word with subtype Theme or Header Footer, while body layouts use subtype Body. Themes use a Word template file.
- Enable and disable keys at runtime (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): A key can be defined with Enabled set to false and enabled by code at runtime. This suits features most customers do not use.
- Guidance for Copilot-friendly extensions (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): A Microsoft Learn article gives guidelines for building extensions that Copilot and agents can work with more easily, for example more descriptive ones.
- ITestHandler interface (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): The interface offers before and after hooks at codeunit, procedure and test case level. All have default implementations.
- Recent records virtual table (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): The recent records list is exposed to AL as a queryable virtual table. Records can be deleted, otherwise it is read only.
- Migration from test toolkit events to test handlers (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): Test handlers are separate from the test toolkit events. Users of those events must migrate to get the new functionality.
- Boolean expressions for Hide if (announced, 1 min, Reporting and analytics): Later you will set a boolean expression on data set values to hide or show content. A small formula language will be part of it.
- BC-Bench bug fixing category (GA (implied), 1 min, Developer tools): Agents fix bugs in the real codebase across 101 tasks from bugs human engineers fixed.
- Admin center API for PTE operations (GA (implied), 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Endpoints for all demoed PTE operations are available in the admin center API. S2S apps used by partners do not need in-environment registration and permission sets to upload and install PTEs.
- API overview page (GA (implied), 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): A new API overview page, shipping in version 29, is the easiest way to find APIs. Searching there shows API names and URLs to try them out.
- Fabric integration APIs (preview, 0 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Setup and monitoring data are available as six APIs listed on the API overview page.
- Strongly typed test context (GA (implied), 0 min, Developer tools): The data source returns an ITestContext, but the test can use its own interface for typed test data.
- Match production in admin center API (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The match production configuration operation is supported in the admin center APIs. Developers can automate it in their processes.
- DGML and SARIF export (GA (implied), 0 min, Developer tools): Results export as DGML for humans or SARIF for agents.
- AL graph query language (GA (implied), 0 min, Developer tools): A query language supports complex queries such as all callers of an object or methods touching a table. It is documented on MS Learn.

output.text:
Developers get 67 relevant features in about 108 minutes of video, and most of them circle one idea: your next teammate might be an agent. There is a standalone AL language server, MCP servers for compiling, profiling and snapshot debugging, and BC-Bench to check whether any of it helps. The point is that agents stop grepping text and start reading what the code and the runtime actually do.

The second theme is less shiny but you will touch it sooner: testing and the platform underneath. Data-driven tests and test handlers change how you structure a test suite. Keys can now span base and extension fields, a long-requested item, and table extension fields are stored on the base table.

Watch first: in-environment PTE management is deprecated as of version 30.0. Plan your move to the admin center within about half a year, and do not mix both experiences in one environment. If you use test toolkit events, moving to test handlers is on you. The Fabric items are preview, and most of the rest is generally available.
